column1: ally§Portugal was England's oldest ally, and the treaty binding them has survived six centuries and every war fought in between.§葡萄牙是英格兰最老的**盟友**，把两国捆在一起的条约熬过了六个世纪和其间的每一场战争。§al-（向）+ ly ← lig（捆，同 ligament 韧带）→ 绑在一起
aloof§He kept aloof from office politics for years, and when the layoffs came nobody could remember what he actually did.§他多年**冷眼旁观**办公室政治，等到裁员时没人想得起他到底做什么。§
alter§One clause was altered overnight, and the version the board approved is not the version anyone finally signed.§有一条条款一夜之间被**改动**，董事会批准的版本和最终签字的版本并不是同一份。§
alteration§A single alteration to the schedule pushed every downstream task back a week and cost the project its winter window.§对进度表的一处**改动**把下游每项任务都推后了一周，让项目错过了冬季的窗口期。§
altruism§Pure altruism is rarer than we like to think: most generosity carries some quiet expectation of being remembered.§纯粹的**利他**比我们愿意承认的更少见，多数慷慨都暗含着被记住的期待。§altr（他人，同 alternative 另一个）→ 为别人着想
altruistic§Her decision was genuinely altruistic—she gave the kidney to a stranger and refused to learn his name.§她的决定是真正**无私的**：把肾捐给一个陌生人，还拒绝知道他的名字。§
amalgam§The city is an amalgam of four older towns, and each still keeps its own festival, dialect, and football rivalry.§这座城市是四个更老城镇的**混合体**，每一处都还保留着自己的节日、方言和球赛宿怨。§
amalgamate§The two firms amalgamated in March, but a year later the sales teams still filed reports in different systems.§两家公司三月**合并**，可一年后销售团队还在两套不同的系统里交报表。§
amalgamation§The amalgamation of the three departments saved money on paper and cost the university its best two researchers.§三个系的**合并**在账面上省了钱，却让这所大学失去了最好的两位研究者。§
amass§He amassed forty thousand photographs in thirty years, and none of them had ever been printed or shown to anyone.§三十年里他**积攒**了四万张照片，一张也没有冲印过，也没给任何人看过。§a-（向）+ mass（堆）→ 堆成一大堆
amateurish§The forgery was amateurish: the signature ran off the edge, and the canvas was thirty years too young.§这幅赝品**很外行**——签名跑出了画边，画布还比真迹晚了三十年。§
ambiguity§The ambiguity in clause nine let both sides claim victory, which is precisely why the drafters left it there.§第九条里的**含糊**让双方都能宣称胜利，而这正是起草者刻意留下它的原因。§ambi-（两边）+ ig ← ag（走，同 act）→ 两边都走得通

ambivalence§Her ambivalence about the promotion was obvious: she wanted the title badly and dreaded every duty attached to it.§她对升职的**矛盾心理**很明显——极想要那个头衔，又害怕随之而来的每一项职责。§ambi-（两边）+ val（力量，同 valid 有效的）→ 两股力气拉扯
ambivalent§Readers remain ambivalent about the ending, which rescues the hero and simultaneously destroys everything he spent the novel protecting.§读者对这个结局仍**心情矛盾**：它救了主角，同时又毁掉他整本书都在保护的一切。§
ameliorate§Nothing ameliorated the housing shortage until the city changed the zoning rules that had frozen construction for two decades.§直到这座城市改掉冻结建设二十年的分区规定，住房短缺才有所**缓解**。§a-（向）+ melior（更好）→ 变好

amend§Congress amended the bill eleven times, and the text that finally passed bore almost no resemblance to the original draft.§国会对这项法案**修订**了十一次，最终通过的文本与初稿几乎面目全非。§a-（去）+ mend ← mend（缺点，同 mendacious 说谎）→ 去掉毛病
amiable§An amiable host, he remembered which guests disliked each other and seated them a full room apart.§作为一位**和蔼可亲**的主人，他记得哪些客人彼此不睦，把他们安排在屋子的两端。§am（爱，同 amateur 爱好者）→ 招人喜欢
amicability§The amicability of the divorce surprised both families, who had braced for years of lawyers and a fight over the house.§这场离婚的**和睦**让两家人都很意外，他们本已做好打几年官司、抢房子的准备。§
amicable§They reached an amicable settlement in one afternoon, splitting the estate without a single lawyer entering the room.§他们一个下午就达成了**友好的**和解，分完遗产，全程没有一位律师进屋。§am（爱，同 amiable 亲切的）
amorphous§The complaint was too amorphous to answer: it named no date, no decision, and no person responsible.§这份投诉**没有具体形态**，无从回应——没提日期，没提决定，也没提负责人。§a-（无）+ morph（形状，同 metamorphosis 变形）

anachronistic§A clock strikes in Shakespeare's Rome, an anachronistic detail that has bothered editors for four hundred years.§莎士比亚笔下的罗马响起钟声，这个**时代错置**的细节困扰了编者四百年。§ana-（逆）+ chron（时间，同 chronology 年表）→ 时间错位
analogous§The situation is analogous to a bank run: confidence collapses first, and the actual shortage arrives only afterward.§这个局面**类似于**银行挤兑：先崩塌的是信心，真正的短缺随后才到。§ana-（依照）+ log（比例／话，同 logic 逻辑）→ 比例相当

anarchist§The anarchist argued not for chaos but for a society organized entirely without rulers, which most of his critics never bothered to read.§这位**无政府主义者**主张的不是混乱，而是完全没有统治者的社会组织——多数批评者压根没读过。§an-（无）+ arch（统治，同 monarch 君主）

anatomy§The anatomy of the failure is simple: one valve, one missing inspection, and eleven people who assumed someone else had checked.§这次事故的**剖析**很简单——一个阀门，一次漏检，十一个都以为别人查过的人。§ana-（分开）+ tom（切，同 atom 不可切分之物）→ 切开来看
anecdotal§The evidence is anecdotal, not statistical: three friends recovered quickly, so he now recommends the treatment to everyone.§这些证据是**道听途说的**而非统计性的——三个朋友好得快，他就向所有人推荐这个疗法。§

anecdote§She opened with an anecdote about a lost suitcase, and by the third sentence the audience had forgotten it was a lecture.§她以一则关于丢失行李箱的**轶事**开场，讲到第三句，听众已经忘了这是一场讲座。§an-（不）+ ec-（出）+ dot（给，同 anecdote 未公开之事）→ 没发表过的私房故事
animate§A single well-placed question animated a discussion that had been circling the same three points for an hour.§一个问得恰到好处的问题**激活**了整场讨论，此前一小时它一直在同样三个点上打转。§anim（气息／生命，同 animal 动物）→ 吹一口气进去

animosity§The animosity between the two departments predates everyone currently working in them, and nobody can name its original cause.§两个部门之间的**敌意**比现在任何一位在职者的资历都久，谁也说不出最初的起因。§anim（心气，同 animate 赋予生气）→ 心里憋着火
annotate§She annotated the manuscript so heavily that her notes now run longer than the text they were meant to explain.§她给手稿**加注**加得太多，如今注释比它们要解释的正文还长。§an-（向）+ not（记号，同 note 笔记）
anomalous§The anomalous reading appeared on only one sensor, and engineers ignored it for six weeks before the pipeline failed.§这个**反常的**读数只出现在一个传感器上，工程师忽略了六周，管道随后就出了事。§an-（不）+ homal（相同）→ 与其他不一样
anomaly§The planet's orbit showed an anomaly that no known body could explain, so astronomers went looking for one they had not yet seen.§这颗行星的轨道存在一处已知天体无法解释的**异常**，于是天文学家去找一个尚未见过的天体。§
anonymity§Anonymity protected the sources, but it also meant the paper could not prove to readers that the sources existed.§**匿名**保护了消息来源，却也意味着报纸无法向读者证明这些来源确实存在。§an-（无）+ onym（名字，同 synonym 同义词）
antagonist§Every good story needs an antagonist whose reasoning the audience can follow, even while hoping he loses.§每个好故事都需要一个**对手**，他的逻辑观众跟得上，尽管他们希望他输。§ant-（对着）+ agon（斗争）→ 对着干的人
antagonistic§His tone turned antagonistic the moment anyone questioned the numbers, which is why the review took four months.§只要有人质疑数据，他的语气就变得**对立**，这就是评审拖了四个月的原因。§
antagonize§The memo antagonized exactly the people whose cooperation the plan required, and the plan died within a fortnight.§这份备忘录**得罪**的恰恰是计划所需要合作的那批人，方案两周内就夭折了。§
antecedent§The pronoun has no clear antecedent, so a reader cannot tell whether "it" refers to the policy or to the objection.§这个代词没有明确的**先行词**，读者分不清 it 指的是政策还是那条反对意见。§ante-（在前）+ ced（走，同 precede 先于）

anthropocentrism§Anthropocentrism runs through the whole report, which values a forest only by the timber and tourism it can yield.§**人类中心主义**贯穿整份报告，它衡量一片森林的价值只看能出多少木材和旅游收入。§anthropo（人，同 anthropology 人类学）+ centr（中心）
anticipate§Good goalkeepers anticipate the shot rather than react to it, which is why the best saves look almost lazy.§好的守门员**预判**射门而不是对射门做反应，所以最精彩的扑救看上去几乎是懒洋洋的。§ante-（先）+ cip（拿，同 capture 捕获）→ 先一步拿到
anticipation§The anticipation was better than the event: three months of waiting collapsed into ninety unremarkable minutes.§**期待**胜过事件本身——三个月的等待坍缩成九十分钟平淡无奇的时间。§
antipathy§His antipathy to committees is well known, and he has turned down four appointments rather than sit on one.§他对委员会的**反感**尽人皆知，宁可推掉四次任命也不肯进去坐着。§anti-（反）+ path（感情，同 sympathy 同情）

antipode§Winter in Sydney is the antipode of winter in London, which is why the two cities' holiday images look so strange together.§悉尼的冬天是伦敦冬天的**对极**，所以两座城市的节日画面摆在一起才那么怪。§anti-（相对）+ pod（脚，同 podium 讲台）→ 脚对着脚的另一端

antiquarian§An antiquarian by temperament, he could date a doorknob within twenty years and cared nothing for anything made after 1900.§他天生是个**古物研究者**，一枚门把手能断代到二十年内，1900 年后的东西一概不感兴趣。§antiqu（古老，同 antique 古董）

antithesis§Her method is the antithesis of his: she tests one variable at a time, while he changes everything and looks at the result.§她的方法是他的**对立面**——她一次只测一个变量，他则全改一遍再看结果。§anti-（相对）+ thesis（放置，同 thesis 论点）→ 摆在对面的说法

apathetic§Voters were not angry but apathetic, and turnout fell below thirty percent for the first time in the district's history.§选民不是愤怒而是**冷漠**，投票率首次跌破百分之三十，这在该选区历史上还是头一回。§a-（无）+ path（感情，同 sympathy 同情）
apathy§Apathy killed the proposal more surely than opposition would have: no one argued against it, and no one showed up.§**冷漠**比反对更彻底地杀死了这项提案——没人反驳它，也没人到场。§
aphorism§"The map is not the territory" is an aphorism worth a chapter, and most people who quote it have read neither.§「地图不是疆域」是一句抵得上一整章的**格言**，多数引用它的人两样都没读过。§apo-（离开）+ hor（界限）→ 划出边界的一句话
aplomb§She handled the interruption with such aplomb that half the audience assumed the heckler had been part of the script.§她**泰然自若**地处理了那次打断，半数观众以为起哄者本就是剧本的一部分。§
apolitical§He insists the foundation is apolitical, yet every grant it made last year went to the same senator's home district.§他坚称这家基金会**不涉政治**，可去年发出的每一笔资助都流向了同一位参议员的选区。§
apologetic§Her apologetic tone undercut a report that was, on the evidence, entirely correct and badly needed saying.§她**满是歉意**的语气削弱了一份报告，而从证据看它完全正确，且极有必要说出来。§
appall§The conditions in the ward appalled the inspector, who filed an emergency order before he had finished the walkthrough.§病房的状况让这位巡查员**震骇不已**，他还没走完就下了紧急整改令。§ap-（向）+ pall（变苍白，同 pale 苍白）→ 吓白了脸
apparition§The apparition in the doorway turned out to be a coat on a hook, but it took him ten minutes to stop shaking.§门口的那个**幻影**原来是挂钩上的一件外套，可他花了十分钟才不再发抖。§ap-（向）+ par（出现，同 appear 出现）

appease§Concessions meant to appease the strikers only convinced them the company had more room to give, and the walkout continued.§旨在**安抚**罢工者的让步反而让他们确信公司还有余地，罢工继续了下去。§ap-（向）+ peas ← pac（和平，同 peace 和平）→ 使平静
apportionment§The apportionment of seats follows population, so a single census error can cost a state representation for ten years.§席位的**分配**依人口而定，因此一次人口普查的差错就能让一个州十年少一个代表。§
apprehend§Police apprehended the suspect at the border, three weeks after he had convinced everyone he was already abroad.§警方在边境**逮捕**了嫌疑人，此时他让所有人相信他已出境已有三周。§ap-（向）+ prehend（抓，同 comprehend 领会）
apprehensive§She was apprehensive about the results for a week, and the letter, when it came, took four seconds to read.§她**惴惴不安**地等了一周结果，而那封信真来时，读完只用了四秒。§
approximate§The figure is approximate: the survey covered one district in four, and the rest was estimated from tax records.§这个数字是**大致的**——普查只覆盖了四分之一的区，其余从税务记录推算。§ap-（向）+ proxim（最近，同 proximity 邻近）
apt§She is apt to answer a question with a better question, which makes her difficult to interview and worth interviewing.§她**惯于**用一个更好的问题回答问题，这让她难采访，也值得采访。§apt（拿住／合适，同 adapt 适应）
arable§Only a third of the valley is arable; the rest is either too steep to plow or too salty to grow anything.§这条河谷只有三分之一**可耕**，其余不是陡得没法犁，就是碱得种不出东西。§ar（耕）

arbitration§Binding arbitration settled the dispute in six weeks, though both sides later agreed the arbitrator had understood neither business.§有约束力的**仲裁**六周就解决了争端，尽管双方后来都认为仲裁员两边的业务都不懂。§arbit（裁判，同 arbitrary 专断的）
arboreal§Sloths are so thoroughly arboreal that they descend to the ground roughly once a week and are nearly helpless there.§树懒**树栖**得如此彻底，大约一周才下地一次，而且在地上几乎毫无自保能力。§arbor（树）
arcane§The rules of the tournament are arcane enough that new players lose on technicalities they have never heard of.§这项赛事的规则**晦涩神秘**到新手常因从未听说的细则而输掉比赛。§arcan（藏起来的，同 ark 柜子）

archaic§The statute uses archaic language that no court has interpreted since 1911, which is why nobody is sure what it forbids.§这条法规使用的是**古旧的**措辞，自 1911 年起再无法院解释过，所以没人确定它究竟禁止什么。§arch（古老／起初，同 archaeology 考古学）

archetypal§He is the archetypal second son of Victorian novels: charming, unemployed, and certain that money will arrive from somewhere.§他是维多利亚小说里**典型原型**式的次子——迷人、无业，且笃信钱总会从什么地方来。§arch（第一／原初）+ type（型）
archive§The paper archived every issue since 1878, and that decision now earns it more than the print edition ever did.§这家报纸**存档**了 1878 年以来的每一期，如今这个决定带来的收入超过了纸质版历来的收入。§
ardor§His ardor for the cause lasted exactly as long as it stayed unpopular; the moment it won, he found another.§他对这项事业的**热忱**恰好持续到它不再冷门为止——它一胜利，他就另找了一个。§ard（燃烧，同 arson 纵火）
arduous§The climb is arduous rather than dangerous: no technical skill is needed, only the willingness to walk uphill for eleven hours.§这段攀登**艰辛**而非危险——不需要技术，只需要愿意连着上坡走十一个小时。§ardu（陡峭）
aroma§The aroma of roasting coffee reaches the far end of the street, and the shop has never spent a cent on advertising.§烘咖啡的**香气**能飘到街那头，这家店从没在广告上花过一分钱。§
aromatic§Aromatic herbs were strewn across the floors of medieval halls, less for pleasure than to cover what lay beneath them.§中世纪厅堂的地上撒满**芳香的**草药，与其说为享受，不如说为掩盖底下的东西。§
